title: Ecosyste.ms Services: advisories, funding, curated lists
description: The smaller **ecosyste.ms** services in one graph: who maintains open-source software, who pays for it, and what is known to be vulnerable in it.
- **35,574 security advisories** (`eco:Advisory`) with severity, CVSS, EPSS and blast radius, linked to the **packages** they affect (`eco:affectsPackage`).
- **39,579 GitHub Sponsors accounts** (`eco:SponsorAccount`) with sponsor counts and minimum tiers.

- **108,722 Open Collective projects** and the collectives that fund them (`eco:fundsProject`): 3,957 funders, of which the 2,739 the collectives endpoint lists (`eco:Collective`) carry donations and balance.
- **10,394 awesome lists** and **1,241 awesome topics** (SKOS labels, aliases, related topics).
- **7,014 Open Sustainable Technology projects** (same schema as `ecosyste-ms-science`) with their packages and repository; 2,937 of them carry a field (`eco:inField`).

Modelled with the Ecosyste.ms Graph Ontology (<https://w3id.org/rete/ecosystems>), which the file carries. Entities sit at canonical IRIs — a repository at its own URL, an account at `https://github.com/{login}`, a collective at `https://opencollective.com/{slug}`, a package at `…/ecosystems/package/{ecosystem}/{name}` — so this graph merges with `ecosyste-ms-science` and `ecosyste-ms-papers` without `owl:sameAs`.

Harvested from the ecosyste.ms public APIs on 2026-08-12 (raw responses: <https://data.graphplaza.com/sources/ecosyste-ms-services/>). Completeness is checked as distinct ids against each API's own total, not pages × page size. Open Collective projects reach 99.6 % of upstream (108,722 of 109,146) through a partitioned, iterate-to-closure pass. `awesome/projects`, `repos`, `packages`, `commits` and `issues` are out of scope by size.

Converted by `scripts/ecosyste_ms/services_to_nt.py` and built with `rete build --strict`, which refuses any IRI the N-Triples grammar or RFC 3987 rejects. Free-text URL fields are escaped where escaping preserves the meaning (11 statements: a `[`/`]` or a second `#`), and **dropped and counted** where no escaping can make them an IRI: one statement, a sponsor homepage written `https://::1` (an IPv6 address without brackets). Values that are not `http(s)` URLs at all were never emitted. The converter prints the tally on every run.
Upstream text is kept as-is; dates are `xsd:dateTime` as the APIs give them. Licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 — attribute "Ecosyste.ms" (https://ecosyste.ms).
example_queries:
# Most-starred repositories behind projects an Open Collective funds
PREFIX eco: <https://w3id.org/rete/ecosystems#>
SELECT ?repo ?stars ?collective WHERE {
  ?collective eco:fundsProject ?p .
  ?p eco:hasRepository ?repo .
  ?repo eco:stars ?stars .
} ORDER BY DESC(?stars) LIMIT 20
